content.thinking:
I need to avoid writing any actual figures myself, using placeholders instead for things like identifiers and durations, while keeping labels and port names as-is. The core symptom here is that users didn't notice real impact, but the metrics themselves stopped arriving entirely.

Tracing the chain: alerts fired when metrics stopped, but shoppers saw no rise in errors, which means the scrape target stopped matching after a new deployment revision renamed a port from one label to another in the production config. I'm noting the missing evidence around why that rename went uncaught, listing contributing factors like the lack of a pre-deploy check for scrape selector matching and the delay before alerting fires, then tracking what needs new action items versus what remains an open assumption — particularly whether rollback actually restored scraping versus just being inferred from the service becoming readable again.

action_items.item: Add a pre-deploy or CI check that renders io-shop's values and verifies that the scrape port name matches what the service-monitor or scrape selector expects, failing the release on mismatch.
Add a post-deploy gate that confirms io-shop's scrape target is present and returning samples shortly after rollout, and rolls back or pages automatically if it is not.

causal_chain.step: The MetricsAbsent alert fired: no samples had arrived from io-shop for {A2} since {A1}, against a one-minute scrape interval. The shop itself was not visibly failing: logs show only routine client-disconnect errors and normal page renders, and the error rate did not rise above its pre-incident level.
The metrics stopped because the scraper no longer matched io-shop's metrics endpoint after the new revision came up. The metric series ended just before the new revision's rollout.

The scrape target stopped matching because the deploy renamed the scrape port from 'metrics' to 'http-metrics' in io-shop's production values, and the scraper keys on the port name. This was the only production change in the window and coincided with the onset.
Rolling the deployment back restored the old revision, and the service could be read again, which supports the deploy as the cause.

contributing_factors.factor: Nothing checked before or during release that the scraper's port-name selector still matched the port declared in the new values. A rename of the port silently disconnected monitoring.

Detection relied on the absence alert, which fires only after several minutes without samples, so the shop ran unmonitored for some time before anyone knew. The deploy itself raised no signal about missing metrics.

input.executive_summary: Monitoring stopped receiving metrics from the shop right after a routine release. The alert fired because the data stopped, not because shoppers were failing. The record shows no rise in failed requests: the error rate stayed at the level seen before the release. The metrics gap lasted at least {duration}, a lower bound because the service had not been seen recovering when metrics were last read. Argus rolled the release back, confirmed the service could be read again, and closed its response after {held}. The real exposure was that the shop was unmonitored for that period, so a real fault would not have been seen.

got_lucky: The shop kept serving normally while it was unmonitored; a real fault in that window would have gone unseen.
The recorded metrics stop well before the end, so recovery of the metrics themselves was not directly observed in the data read.
went_well: Argus tied the metrics gap to the only production change in the window and rolled it back within seconds of the alert.
The Investigator read the logs and recognised that shoppers were still being served normally, so the incident was treated as a monitoring gap rather than an outage.
went_wrong: A port rename passed review and release without any check that monitoring would still find the service.
The alert reached Argus only after the series had already been absent for {A2}.

input.root_cause: A production deploy renamed the Prometheus scrape port in io-shop's values from 'metrics' to 'http-metrics'. The component that scrapes io-shop matches targets by port name, so it stopped matching and collection ceased, while the shop kept serving. Nothing before release checked that the monitoring configuration still matched the renamed port.
input.symptom: Shop metrics stopped arriving, leaving monitoring blind
